card.name: Sonderhoning
card.era: Oldest tunes from the 1700s; continuous ~300-year tradition
card.tagline: Maritime couple dance from Fano island.
card.profile: Sonderhoning is a traditional couple dance and melody type from the village of Sonderho on the island of Fano off Denmark's west coast. The dance is a pols (a three-step turning couple dance in a circle) and is notable because the dance is in 3/4 while the melodies are most often in 2/4. It has a walking/promenade part (gangtrin) and a turning part, danced with a special hold; music is traditionally played on the fiddle, the repertoire carried for five to six generations by the Sonnichsen and Brinch families. It is the social centerpiece of Sonderho festivities, danced in traditional Fano costume (Danish Wikipedia; Fonden Gamle Sonderho; Univ. of Toronto folk-dance archive).
card.insight: Per Fonden Gamle Sonderho, Sonderho is the only community in Denmark with a living music-and-dance tradition traceable ~300 years that never fell out of use; the foundation applied in 2018 for UNESCO listing, but it is not inscribed.
card.image_significance: Fanø's seafaring polska in 2/4. A representative image shows the characteristic movement and dress of the tradition — Fanø, Denmark.
